title: Japan's Convenience Stores Launch AI-Designed Sweets
paragraphs: Would you try a sweet created by AI? If you live in Japan, you'll have plenty of chances. But beware — some might contain things you wouldn't normally find in a dessert, like pickles!
Japanese convenience store chains Lawson and FamilyMart are both using AI to come up with new product ideas.

Lawson will start selling three AI-designed products on September 29 at about 4,700 stores in Tokyo and the surrounding areas. They include a pickle-flavored lemon tart; bread filled with red bean paste, butter and yogurt; and a savory salad made to look like a parfait!
The company asked generative AI to suggest surprising flavor combinations that would make customers pause and think, "What is this?" Though the ideas also had to taste good!

Interestingly, Lawson did not give the AI data on past sales or market trends. It wanted ideas that were not limited by what had sold well before. However, humans still did the important work of testing the ideas and adjusting the taste, appearance and quality.

FamilyMart took a different approach. It gave sales data to AI and asked it to come up with something that felt new but also had a good chance of being popular. AI was used to generate ideas, while humans created the final product.

The result was a sweet potato canelé — a small baked French pastry — topped with caramel sauce. The dessert will go on sale across Japan on September 22 as part of the chain's autumn sweet potato campaign.

This isn't FamilyMart's first experiment with AI. In July, it tested a biscuit sandwich filled with thick milk cream. The product sold well, and FamilyMart now plans to sell 10 sweets based on AI-generated ideas by the end of March 2027.
But while AI may have plenty of ideas, it's shoppers who get to decide whether pickles really belong in a lemon tart!
